newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-May 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-May 16.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- Eleven revisions were made by post-handover leader Tung Chee-hwa's office to the bills to amend two civil liberties ordinances after Hong Kong reverts to China on July 1. Political parties with seats on the post-handover provisional legislature supported the revisions, while the Democratic Party and human rights groups attacked the changes.
-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- Red chip share prices dropped due to speculation mainland authorities might take measures to stem the inflow of funds to Hong Kong.

-- WEN WEI PO -- Chinese President Jiang Zemin met visiting French President Jacques Chirac. China and France signed contracts worth more than US$3 billion during Chirac's visit, and agreed to establish a partner relationship.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- A television series about the Hong Kong garrison of China's People's Liberation Army began filming recently. Jointly produced by Beijing's CCTV and the military department of Guangdong province, the eight-episode series will focus on building up the image of the garrison. The first four episodes will be shown on CCTV before the handover.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Thai authorities took their revenge on overseas hedge funds attacking the baht by sharply cranking up offshore interest rates, leaving "blood on the floor" at some hedge fund offices.
-- Shanghai-based Shenyin & Wanguo Securities and Haitong Securities are to challenge charges brought by China's national securities watchdog that they participated in improper trading.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Former director of China's Xinhua news agency, Xu Jiatun, made an open appeal to the Chinese leadership to restore the freedoms of disgraced former party chief Zhao Zeyang before the Communist Party holds its 15th National Congress.
